title: Trip Cost Per Person Calculator: Split Any Total
description: Divide any shared trip total by the group size with the Trip Cost Per Person Calculator — the per-person budget in one division. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a $1,240 trip shared by five people is $248 each — the number group chats are actually asking for when they say 'so what do I owe?'
quick_answer: The Trip Cost Per Person Calculator divides a trip's shared total by the number of people travelling and returns the equal per-person amount. Enter the total — fuel, stays, food, the lot, or just one shared pot — and the headcount, and read what each person owes the plan.

popular_table.title: Totals per person
popular_table.intro: Equal shares of common trip totals — the table group chats wish they had open.
popular_table.note: Equal shares assume equal participation. Part-way riders and exempt drivers are handled by splitting per leg — the principle generalises, the arithmetic stays this simple.

faq: Does it handle unequal shares?
The built-in split is equal. For unequal (part-way riders, one person treating), split the relevant legs separately and add each person's — the even split is the building block.
What costs should I include?
Whatever the group agreed to share: fuel, stays, shared food, tolls. The deal precedes the division; this page does the dividing.
Does the route include live traffic?
No — this divides a total, which already contains whatever the road did to you.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
It shaped the total you are dividing. The division itself is gloriously distance-free.
Can route results change over time?
Totals change as plans do; recompute at booking time and again at the trip's end. The final split uses final numbers.
Rounding left cents over.
Shares round to cents; the remainder conventionally stays in the kitty for the last coffee. Name the convention once and it never argues again.
Children count as people?
Your group's call — many count children at half or exempt the hosts' kids. Enter the headcount your deal defines.
Someone pays for everyone — still useful?
Yes: the per-person figure becomes the thank-you debt each traveller owes the payer, to the cent.
Different currencies mid-trip?
Convert the total first, then divide. Splitting across exchange rates is how friendships acquire spreadsheets.
The group size changes mid-trip.
Split by segments: each segment's costs over its own headcount. Fairness is per-leg, like everything else on the road.
